question: A 14-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of a 1-month history of pain in his right leg. His mother has been giving him ketorolac at night to improve his sleep, but the pain has not improved. Physical examination shows marked tenderness along the right mid-femur. An x-ray of the right lower extremity shows several lytic lesions in the diaphysis of the femur and a surrounding cortex covered by several layers of new bone. A biopsy of the right femur shows small round blue cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of pain in the right leg, marked tenderness along the mid-femur, lytic lesions in the femur diaphysis, surrounding new bone formation, and biopsy showing small round blue cells are highly suggestive of Ewing sarcoma. The evidence paths of soreness to touch in the right lower extremity and the relationship between bone abnormalities and biopsy findings support this diagnosis.
analysis: The patient's presentation of pain in the right leg, marked tenderness along the mid-femur, lytic lesions in the femur diaphysis, surrounding new bone formation, and biopsy showing small round blue cells are highly indicative of Ewing sarcoma. Ewing sarcoma is a malignant bone tumor that commonly affects children and adolescents, presenting with similar features as described in this case.
